prompt: In the fraction 3/5, what is the top number called?
rationale: The numerator is above the fraction bar; the denominator is below it.

prompt: In a fraction describing equal parts of a whole, what does the denominator tell you?
answers: How many equal parts make up the whole
How many of those parts are selected
How many whole items are always present
How many separate numbers have been added
rationale: The denominator specifies the division into equal parts; the numerator counts the parts represented.

prompt: Which of these is a proper fraction?
rationale: A positive proper fraction has numerator smaller than denominator, hence value below one.

prompt: Which fraction has the same value as 1/2?
rationale: Multiplying both numerator and denominator by two gives two quarters.

prompt: Which of these is a unit fraction?
rationale: A unit fraction has numerator one and a positive integer denominator; only one seventh meets that definition.

prompt: What separates the whole-number part from the fractional part in decimal notation such as 12.5?
rationale: In this notation the point separates whole units from decimal fractional places.

prompt: What does the digit 4 represent in the decimal 0.4?
rationale: The first position to the right of the decimal point is tenths.

prompt: Which of these decimal numbers is largest?
rationale: Eight tenths is greater than eighteen hundredths, eight hundredths and eight thousandths.

prompt: What does percent mean?
rationale: Percent expresses a ratio to one hundred.

prompt: Which fraction of a whole is 25%?
rationale: Twenty-five out of one hundred simplifies to one quarter.

prompt: A progress bar is 100% complete. What fraction of the task is finished?
rationale: One hundred percent represents one whole in this stated completion context.

prompt: When a positive fraction is in simplest form, what is true of its numerator and denominator?
answers: They have no common factor greater than 1
rationale: A reduced fraction has relatively prime numerator and denominator.

prompt: Which of these is an improper fraction?
rationale: The numerator five exceeds the denominator three; the other fractions are positive and below one.

prompt: Which of these is written as a mixed number?
rationale: Two and one third has both a whole-number part and a proper fractional part.

prompt: Which fraction equals the decimal 0.75?
rationale: Seventy-five hundredths reduces to three quarters.

prompt: Which of these numbers is closest to zero?
rationale: Among these negative integers, minus two has the smallest absolute value.

prompt: Which of these whole numbers is odd?
rationale: Seventeen is not divisible by two; the other choices are.

prompt: What makes an integer even?
answers: It is divisible by 2 without a remainder
rationale: Even integers are multiples of two, including zero and negative multiples.

prompt: What is the value of the digit 5 in the number 5,274?
rationale: Five occupies the thousands place.

prompt: What does squaring a number mean?
rationale: A square is the product of two equal factors; doubling is different.

prompt: What does 4 cubed mean?
rationale: Cubing uses the number as a factor three times, not multiplying by three.

prompt: For nonnegative numbers, which operation reverses squaring?
rationale: Restricting to nonnegative numbers makes principal square root the inverse of squaring.

prompt: In ordinary real-number arithmetic, what is 8 divided by 0?
rationale: No real number multiplied by zero gives eight, so this division is undefined.

prompt: In the division 20 ÷ 4 = 5, which number is the dividend?
rationale: The dividend is the amount being divided, here twenty.

prompt: What is the result of a division called?
rationale: Quotient is the result of division; product, sum and difference belong to other operations.

prompt: What is an equilateral triangle?
answers: A triangle with all three sides equal
A triangle with all three sides unequal
Any triangle containing a right angle
Any triangle with a curved side
rationale: Equilateral describes equality of all three side lengths.

prompt: In an isosceles triangle, at least how many sides are equal in length?
rationale: At least two sides are equal; the question works with both inclusive and exclusive conventions.

prompt: How many degrees are in a right angle?
rationale: A right angle is one quarter of a full turn.

prompt: Which of these is an acute angle?
rationale: An acute angle is greater than zero and less than ninety degrees.

prompt: Which of these is an obtuse angle?
rationale: An obtuse angle lies strictly between ninety and one hundred eighty degrees.

prompt: How many degrees are in a straight angle?
rationale: A straight angle is a half-turn.

prompt: Which of these is a reflex angle?
rationale: A reflex angle is greater than one hundred eighty and less than three hundred sixty degrees.

prompt: In ordinary Euclidean geometry, what is the sum of the three interior angles of a triangle?
rationale: The Euclidean qualification excludes triangles on curved surfaces.

prompt: What is true of distinct parallel straight lines in a flat plane?
answers: They meet at a right angle
rationale: Distinct coplanar parallel lines do not intersect in Euclidean geometry.

prompt: At what angle do perpendicular straight lines meet?
rationale: Perpendicular lines intersect at a right angle.

prompt: What is a radius of a circle?
answers: A line segment from its centre to its circumference
A segment joining any two boundary points
The full distance around the circle
The area enclosed by the circle
rationale: A radius connects the centre with a point on the circular boundary.

prompt: A circle has radius r. How long is its diameter?
rationale: A diameter passes through the centre and has twice the radius length.

prompt: What is the distance all the way around a circle called?
rationale: Circumference is the circular perimeter.

prompt: What is a chord of a circle?
answers: A straight segment joining two points on the circle
Only the distance from the centre to the edge
The whole region inside the circle
The area of half the circle
rationale: A chord has both endpoints on the circle; a diameter is a special chord.

prompt: How many lines of reflection symmetry does a square have?
rationale: Two diagonals and the two lines through opposite side midpoints give four.

prompt: How many faces does a cube have?
rationale: A cube has six square faces, eight vertices and twelve edges.

prompt: How many vertices, or corners, does a rectangular cuboid have?
rationale: A cuboid has eight corner vertices.

prompt: Which solid has two parallel circular ends and a curved side?
rationale: A circular cylinder has two matching circular ends.

prompt: Which solid has a circular base and narrows to a single point?
rationale: A cone has a circular base and an apex.

prompt: The surface of an ideal ball has which geometric shape?
rationale: A sphere is the surface of an ideal ball; the enclosed solid is called a ball in formal geometry.

prompt: Which description defines a polygon?
answers: A closed flat shape bounded by straight line segments
Any circle drawn with a compass
rationale: Polygons are closed plane figures with straight segment boundaries.

prompt: How many sides does a pentagon have?
rationale: The prefix penta indicates five sides.

prompt: How many sides does an octagon have?
rationale: An octagon has eight sides.

prompt: What is a tessellation of a flat surface?
answers: A covering by shapes with no gaps or overlaps
Any set of shapes separated by large gaps
Only one circle drawn in the centre
A pile of cubes stacked vertically
rationale: A tessellation tiles the plane without gaps or overlapping interiors.

prompt: What does the perimeter of a flat shape measure?
answers: The total length around its boundary
The amount of space inside it
The length of its longest diagonal
rationale: Perimeter is boundary length, not area or volume.

prompt: What is the result of adding numbers called?
rationale: A sum is an addition result.

prompt: What is the result of subtracting one number from another called?
rationale: Subtraction gives a difference.

prompt: What is the result of multiplying numbers called?
rationale: Multiplication gives a product.

prompt: What is the remainder in a whole-number division?
answers: The amount left after making as many equal groups as possible
The result of multiplying the two starting numbers
rationale: A remainder is the amount not included in the complete equal groups.

prompt: What does the equals sign in a mathematical statement mean?
answers: Both sides have the same value
The left side is always larger
The right side must be zero
rationale: Equality asserts that the expressions on either side represent the same value.

prompt: Which mathematical symbol means greater than?
rationale: Greater-than points its open side towards the larger expression.

prompt: Which mathematical symbol means less than?
rationale: Less-than indicates that the expression on the left is smaller.

prompt: What does the symbol ≠ mean?
rationale: The crossed equals sign indicates inequality, not approximate equality.

prompt: What does the symbol ≈ usually mean?
answers: Exactly equal to in every decimal place
rationale: Approximate equality is used for rounded or estimated values.

prompt: In an expression such as 2 × (3 + 4), what do the brackets group together?
rationale: The bracketed expression is treated as a group and evaluated before the outside multiplication.

prompt: Which operation is represented by the symbol ×?
rationale: The cross symbol denotes multiplication in this arithmetic context.

prompt: Which operation is represented by the symbol ÷?
rationale: The obelus denotes division.

prompt: On a conventional horizontal number line, numbers become larger in which direction?
rationale: The usual horizontal orientation increases from left to right.

prompt: Is zero a positive number, a negative number, or neither?
rationale: Zero is neither strictly positive nor strictly negative.

prompt: Which of these numbers is an integer?
rationale: Integers include negative and positive whole-number values and zero, but not nonwhole fractions.

prompt: In ordinary decimal notation, what is a digit?
answers: Any number with exactly two figures
rationale: Digits are the ten basic symbols used to write decimal numerals.

prompt: How many different digits are used in ordinary decimal notation?
rationale: The digit symbols zero through nine total ten.

prompt: What is 64 rounded to the nearest ten?
rationale: Sixty-four is four away from sixty and six away from seventy.

prompt: Which is the closest estimate to 41 + 58?
rationale: The exact sum is ninety-nine, nearest to one hundred among the choices.

prompt: What does arranging numbers in ascending order mean?
answers: Putting all odd numbers first regardless of size
Putting zero last in every list
rationale: Ascending order increases in value.

prompt: What does arranging numbers in descending order mean?
answers: Putting all even numbers first regardless of size
Putting negative numbers last in every list
rationale: Descending order decreases in value.

prompt: Which of these is a multiple of 6?
rationale: Eighteen is six times three; the other values are not divisible by six.

prompt: Which of these is a factor of 20?
rationale: Twenty divided by five gives a whole-number quotient of four.

prompt: How many positive factors does a prime number have?
rationale: A prime has precisely two distinct positive factors: one and itself.

prompt: What is a composite positive integer?
answers: An integer greater than 1 with more than two positive factors
An integer with exactly two positive factors
Only a number written with two digits
rationale: Composite positive integers greater than one are nonprime and have additional positive factors.

prompt: On a standard Cartesian coordinate graph, which way does the x-axis run?
rationale: The standard Cartesian x-axis is horizontal.

prompt: On a standard Cartesian coordinate graph, which way does the y-axis run?
rationale: The standard Cartesian y-axis is vertical.

prompt: What are the coordinates of the origin on a standard Cartesian graph?
rationale: The two coordinate axes cross at the origin, where both coordinates are zero.

prompt: From the origin, how do you locate the point (3, 2) on a standard Cartesian graph?
answers: Move 3 units right and 2 units up
Move 2 units right and 3 units up
Move 3 units left and 2 units down
Move 3 units up and 2 units left
rationale: The first coordinate is horizontal displacement and the second vertical displacement.

prompt: In the usual tally-mark system, a diagonal stroke across four upright strokes makes a group of how many?
rationale: Four upright marks crossed by a fifth stroke represent five.

prompt: A fair coin has one head side and one tail side. What is the probability of heads on one toss?
rationale: The two outcomes are equally likely, so heads has probability one half.

prompt: What probability is assigned to an impossible event?
rationale: An impossible event has probability zero.

prompt: What probability is assigned to an event that is certain to happen?
rationale: A certain event has probability one, equivalent to one hundred percent.

prompt: A probability written as a decimal must lie in which interval?
rationale: Probabilities cannot be below zero or above one.

prompt: A bag contains 3 red counters and 1 blue counter. Each counter is equally likely to be chosen. Which colour is more likely?
rationale: Three of four counters are red, so red is more likely than blue.

prompt: What is the smallest number in the list 8, 7, 10, 5?
rationale: Comparing all four values gives a minimum of five.

prompt: A shop bill is £1.95 plus £2.10. Which is the closest whole-pound estimate of the total?
rationale: The exact total is four pounds and five pence, nearest to four pounds.

prompt: A film starts at 10:20. What time is it 30 minutes later?
rationale: Adding thirty minutes to twenty past ten gives ten fifty.

prompt: How much time passes from 14:00 to 15:15 on the same day?
rationale: From fourteen to fifteen is one hour, followed by fifteen minutes.

prompt: How many millilitres make 1 litre?
rationale: Milli denotes one thousandth, so a litre contains one thousand millilitres.

prompt: How many centimetres make 1 metre?
rationale: Centi denotes one hundredth, giving one hundred centimetres per metre.

prompt: How many grams make 1 kilogram?
rationale: Kilo denotes one thousand, so a kilogram contains one thousand grams.

prompt: Which units would normally describe the area of a floor?
rationale: Area is two-dimensional and measured in square units.

prompt: Which units would normally describe the volume of a room?
rationale: Volume measures three-dimensional space using cubic units.

prompt: Which instrument is commonly used to measure an angle drawn on paper?
rationale: A protractor measures angles; compasses construct circles and transfer distances.

prompt: What does a pair of drawing compasses keep fixed while drawing a circle?
answers: The distance from its centre to its boundary
The length of every other line on the page
The thickness of the drawing paper
The angle between every pair of separate lines
rationale: The fixed compass opening maintains a constant radius.

prompt: On a map, 1 centimetre represents 1 kilometre. What distance does 3 centimetres represent?
rationale: The specified scale gives one kilometre for each centimetre, so three represent three kilometres.

prompt: You pay £5 for an item costing £3.40. How much change should you receive?
rationale: Five pounds minus three pounds forty is one pound sixty.

prompt: You answer 8 out of 10 questions correctly. What percentage is that?
rationale: Eight tenths is eighty hundredths, hence eighty percent.

prompt: Red and blue counters are in the ratio 2:1. There are 9 counters altogether. How many are blue?
rationale: The three ratio parts each contain three counters; blue occupies one part.
